name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,452

clue.text: Slashes and strikes head off

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone lopping things and chopping off a head, perhaps an executioner at work.
explanation.walkthrough: WHACKS loses its W to leave HACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to cut roughly with heavy chopping blows, which is what slashing does too.

clue.text: Has curtailed ill-temper about bill relating to decent housing

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the word loses its tail end
about means going round, so the temper word wraps the bill word

blocks.note: bile stands for bad temper or irritability
a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A grumpy tenant fussing over a bill for their accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has curtailed' looks like a verb phrase, but it just means the word has, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitable building is fit to live in, the standard a decent home must meet.

clue.text: Sport: strain in playing etc

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them
in places the strain word inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to rick is to sprain or strain a joint

explanation.surface: Pulling a muscle while playing sport and all the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A crick in the neck tempts as the strain, but here it is a rick, a sprain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game played between two elevens, a sport.

clue.text: Henry, interrupting Samuel, is 23

indicators.note: something interrupting another breaks into its middle

blocks.note: Sam is the short form of Samuel
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry barging in while Samuel speaks, with a cross-reference finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to 23-down, BOGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake, and a sham is likewise a counterfeit or pretence.

clue.text: Dickens, perhaps, about first in reading material, primarily at this time of year

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for a noun; the puzzle appeared at the festive season

indicators.note: primarily asks for the leading letters of the words it follows
in places one piece inside the opening letters
about means the name goes around the rest

blocks.note: Chas is the old abbreviation of Charles, as in Charles Dickens
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Reading Dickens, A Christmas Carol perhaps, is a seasonal tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: IST (1st) goes inside R and M, and CHAS wraps the lot. 'Dickens' tempts as an oath, but it is the author's first name abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle ran in December, so the festive season is the time of year the setter means.

clue.text: I'm engaged in game, dismissing a second ringing of bell?

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so one piece sits inside the other
dismissing sends a letter away from the word

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone absorbed in a game who is distracted by a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two S's in the game goes; it does not matter which.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimes are the musical sounds of bells being struck; the question mark marks the plural reading.

clue.text: Artist having culture, missing note of esoteric activity

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A cultured artist lacking a musical note, in a highbrow pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied pursuits are refined and select, remote from ordinary interests, which is what esoteric means.

clue.text: 3 vandalised, dropping head in contrition?

indicators.note: dropping its head means losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A vandal caught and made to show remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM is 3-down; DEFACED loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced describes someone looking embarrassed and sorry, the outward sign of contrition.

clue.text: Cunning I observed in French sick of war

indicators.note: something observed in another is seen inside it

blocks.note: mal is French for ill or bad

explanation.surface: Someone in France fed up with fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick of war' reads as weary of fighting, but 'French sick' is the container and 'of war' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial is the adjective for things belonging to warfare and soldiers, as in martial law.

clue.text: Covering prediction of female behaviour?

blocks.note: first meaning: a hard outer casing
second meaning: the contraction of she will, forecasting what a woman will do

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning ignores the apostrophe: SHE'LL predicts what she is going to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is the hard protective casing of an egg, nut or sea creature.

clue.text: Soldier's equipment, notice, put in funeral carriage

indicators.note: put in places the first two pieces inside the carriage word

blocks.note: a rig is a set of equipment
an ad is a public notice

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit and death notice placed on the hearse at a military funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer commanding a brigade, so a soldier.

clue.text: Match about to be held in time

indicators.note: being held in means being enclosed by the following word

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A sports fixture about to be played on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a game; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match correspond with each other, which is what agreeing statements do.

clue.text: Risk overlooking Society's opinion

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so a letter is ignored

blocks.note: to stake something is to risk it

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble by ignoring what society thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: STAKE without its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's take on a subject is their view or interpretation of it.

clue.text: Approach to dieting: fines when found playing with ladle

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them around freely

explanation.surface: A diet club penalises members caught helping themselves from the soup ladle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieting means refusing yourself food you want, a matter of restraint that is the core of the answer.

clue.text: Colt left you once clutching ornate saddle for horse

indicators.note: ornate suggests elaborate decoration, a reworking of the letters
clutching means holding inside, so the archaic pronoun wraps the rearranged letters

blocks.note: c is the abbreviation for colt in racing form
ye is the old form of you
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A young horse that once wore an elaborate saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of draught horse, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Vampire going to part of roof, one escaping conflict

indicators.note: one escaping means a single I gets away from the word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vampire flies to the rooftop to escape a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One escaping' works on the roof piece only.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight between armed forces, a form of armed conflict.

clue.text: Classic hero, male, hurries to encircle lake

indicators.note: encircling means surrounding, so one word goes round a letter

explanation.surface: A mythic hero dashing round a lake, as in one of his labours.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracles is the Greek name of Hercules, the strongman of classical myth.

clue.text: Bungler's scheme ill organised

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An incompetent's plan was badly thought out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'. The word comes from Yiddish.
explanation.definitionFit: A schlemiel is a clumsy, unlucky person who always makes a mess of things.

clue.text: Broker, one thinking to erase first bit of tension

indicators.note: erasing rubs out a letter from the word

explanation.surface: A negotiator trying to calm things by thinking hard.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDITATOR loses its middle T.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker arranges deals between parties, as a mediator negotiates settlements between them.

clue.text: Expressed rejection of award involving Member that's passed on

indicators.note: rejection throws the honour back, so it is read the other way
involving means taking in another piece

blocks.note: OBE is the British honour Officer of the Order of the British Empire
passed on is a euphemism for died

explanation.surface: An MP turns down an honour that came too late, after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody an idea is to give it concrete form, to express or personify it.

clue.text: Something new at the pub - special offer?

blocks.note: a gain is something newly acquired

explanation.surface: A new beer at the local might be a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as BAR GAIN, a pub's acquisition; 'at' places the gain beside the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something sold cheaply, the kind of deal a special offer provides.

clue.text: Show of warmth here, principally?

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the heart stands for affection and warmth of feeling

explanation.surface: Someone pointing to the spot in a home where warmth is chiefly shown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the fireplace is where warmth chiefly shows in a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth is the floor of a fireplace, the main source of warmth in a traditional house.

clue.text: European royal family to come down on one British monarch

explanation.surface: A European royal falls on a British monarch, a fanciful royal collision.
explanation.walkthrough: Rainier was the name of Monaco's princes, Grace Kelly's husband among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruling house of Monaco is the Grimaldis, whose princes included Rainier, so the name stands for that dynasty.

clue.text: Garrick initially puts on Ibsen play

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the name

blocks.note: to host is to put on an event

explanation.surface: The actor David Garrick stages a Norwegian drama.
explanation.walkthrough: David Garrick was the great 18th-century London actor-manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts is an 1881 drama by Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian playwright.

clue.text: Stream spectacle incorporating new celebration of verse

indicators.note: incorporating means taking a letter into its body

blocks.note: burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A poetry festival held beside a picturesque stream.
explanation.definitionFit: On 25 January Scots honour the poet Robert Burns with supper, whisky and recitations of his poems.

clue.text: John, perhaps, is 3

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet, and a bog is the British slang

explanation.surface: A man called John is described as a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: A john is the American word for what the British call a bog, so 'John, perhaps' is a BOG, US. 3 refers to 3-down, SHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake or counterfeit thing, and bogus means fake in the same way.

clue.text: What one has in possession of sentence or sentience?

definitions.text: What one has in possession of sentence or sentience?

blocks.clueFragment: What one has in possession of sentence
blocks.note: surface reading: what you have when you hold a sentence, as words on a page
setter's reading: the long prison sentence, and being alive and aware

explanation.walkthrough: One word fits both: the prisoner serving the longest term, and anyone with sentience, has it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term for the rest of one's days carries the same word as existence itself, the state of a conscious being.

clue.text: Vital clue involves powder

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the letters lie within the phrase

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A detective's crucial lead is some dust found at the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into talcum powder for the skin.

clue.text: Boss consuming article, a fruit

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the boss word takes the article inside

blocks.note: guv, short for governor, is British slang for a boss

explanation.surface: The boss eating a piece of fruit at the desk.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit with pink or white flesh.

clue.text: Italian conductor to search in Italy

blocks.note: to scan is to search over
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Hunting through Italy for a famous maestro.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was the celebrated Italian orchestral conductor of La Scala and the NBC Symphony.

clue.text: More rational to keep cold reserve for white wines

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so a letter goes in the comparative

blocks.note: C for cold, as on taps
res is the abbreviation for reserve

explanation.surface: Sensible advice to chill some wine and hold back the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancerre is a crisp Loire valley white made from Sauvignon Blanc grapes.

clue.text: Exiled European king's men coming back into US state

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so read it backwards
into places the turned piece inside the state abbreviation

blocks.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A deposed king's followers returning to America.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol II of Romania was deposed in 1940 and lived in exile, ending his days in Portugal after time in the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol was the name of Romanian kings, the second of whom abdicated and went into exile.
